item.title: Make listItems follow cursor pagination
item.brief: Change listItems(transport) so it resolves to every item in order by requesting GET /items and following next_cursor until it is null or absent, passing the cursor back unchanged; the first request sends no cursor. Add tests with a fake transport that serves multiple pages, a single page, an absent next_cursor, and checks the cursor is passed unchanged and the first request has no cursor. Update the README to document that listItems pages through the API. Keep `npm test` passing. Commit on the local branch; do not push.

state.summary:
listItems(transport) now follows cursor pagination. It sends GET /items with no cursor first, passes next_cursor back unchanged, stops when next_cursor is null or absent, and returns all items in order. It throws if a response lacks an items array or repeats any cursor, so a cycle fails instead of looping. pr.body: Approach: client.js listItems loops GET /items, first request with no cursor, passing next_cursor back unchanged; a Set of seen cursors rejects any repeat, so A->A and A->B->A throw. Throws if the response lacks an items array. Key files: client.js, test/client.test.js (fake paged transport, 5 new tests), README.md (documents paging). Checks: npm test 9/9 on 0489a9c. Assumptions: the server follows the shared contract (cursor opaque, null or absent on last page). inventory-api not touched. Known gap: no test for a very long non-cyclic chain or an empty-string cursor. Non-blocking nit: while(true)/break loop shape.
pr.summary: listItems now returns every item across pages. now follows next_cursor until null/absent, and rejects cursor cycles. before: first page only, now: all pages in order.

risk.why: Contained behaviour change in client.js listItems only: one call now makes N requests and returns all pages. No API, persistence or security surface changed. Tests run and passing. Review found one blocking gap (A->B->A cycle), fixed and delta-reviewed. Non-blocking nit left open.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief: Implement the GET /items pagination exactly as the shared contract specifies: optional limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor query parameters; body {"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string or null>}; items ordered by id; 400 with {"error": "..."} for an invalid limit or cursor. Add unit tests covering: default page size, limit bounds (0, 101, non-integer), cursor round-trip across pages, last page returns null next_cursor, invalid cursor returns 400, and that every item is returned exactly once across pages. Update the README to document the parameters, response shape and errors. Keep `python3 -m unittest` passing. Commit on the local branch; do not push.

pr.body: Approach: cursor is the id of the last item served, as a string; the next page holds items with a greater id. The cursor must match an item in the catalogue, otherwise 400 'invalid cursor'. Non-string query values (for example JSON numbers from api_cli.py) return 400 instead of raising. Key files: api.py (list_items, parse_limit, parse_cursor), test_api.py (PaginationTest), README.md (endpoint documentation). Checks: python3 -B -m unittest, 10 tests OK on tree 194d7edf. Review: reviewers 1 and 2 passed 2e34fcf; reviewer 3 failed it on the non-string input bug, fixed in 3dc9b5f; the delta reviewer passed 3dc9b5f. Advisory, left open: the default page size of 20 changes output for existing callers and needs a changelog note; the catalogue is sorted on every request (fine at 57 items). Assumptions: the cursor is validated against the current catalogue, so a cursor for a deleted item returns 400. inventory-client is handled by its own item.
pr.summary: Made GET /items paginate with limit and cursor. Now returns at most 20 items by default (limit 1..100) plus next_cursor. Before: every item in one response, no next_cursor. Now: pages of items ordered by id, null next_cursor on the last page, 400 for invalid limit or cursor.
pr.title: feat(api): add cursor pagination to GET /items

risk.why: Public API change: GET /items now returns 20 items by default, which silently truncates responses for existing callers, and adds new 400 paths. Touches api.py, test_api.py and README.md. Behaviour changes; tests added and passing. Reviewer risk levels: high (reviewers 1 and 2), medium on the delta.
